Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, 'Can the Subaltern Speak?', in Marxism and the Interpretation of Culture, ed. Nelson and Grossberg (University of Illinois Press, 1988), argued that the gendered colonial subaltern cannot be recovered through dominant epistemic frames.
Women situated at the intersection of colonial rule and patriarchal structures are often rendered inaudible within the dominant archives and theoretical frameworks that purport to represent them.

Michel Foucault, Discipline and Punish (French ed. Gallimard, 1975; English ed. Pantheon, 1977), traced the historical shift from sovereign spectacle of punishment to disciplinary techniques of the modern prison.

Modern Western societies shifted from public corporal punishment to disciplinary regimes of surveillance, classification, and timetable that train bodies and minds across schools, factories, and prisons.
Laura Mulvey, 'Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema', Screen 16 (1975) 6-18, argued that classical Hollywood cinema structures vision through an active male gaze and passive female image.
Classical Hollywood cinema has typically organized point of view so that the act of looking is coded as masculine and active while women appear as the passive object of that gaze.

Andre Bazin, 'The Ontology of the Photographic Image' (1945), collected in What Is Cinema? vol. 1 (University of California Press, 1967), argued that photography's indexical link to reality underwrites cinema's realist vocation.
Because a photographic image is causally imprinted by light from the object photographed, cinema carries a distinctive commitment to reproducing the contingency and depth of the physical world.

Vladimir Propp, Morphology of the Folktale (Russian original 1928; English trans. University of Texas Press, 1968), identified a fixed sequence of thirty-one narrative functions underlying the Russian wondertale.
Russian wondertales can be analyzed as variations on a limited, ordered sequence of narrative functions such as departure, testing, and return, performed by a small set of character roles.

Mikhail Bakhtin, 'Discourse in the Novel', in The Dialogic Imagination, ed. Holquist (University of Texas Press, 1981), argued that the novel is defined by heteroglossia and the dialogic interplay of social voices.
The novel as a genre is distinguished by its capacity to stage the interaction of many social voices and styles within a single work, rather than imposing a single authoritative discourse.

Fredric Jameson, 'Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism', New Left Review 146 (1984) 53-92, argued that postmodern culture is characterized by pastiche, depthlessness, and a weakening of historicity.
Late twentieth-century culture increasingly relies on pastiche and stylistic quotation, often losing the sense of historical depth and critical distance associated with earlier modernism.

Harold Rosenberg, 'The American Action Painters', ARTnews 51, no. 8 (1952) 22-23, 48-50, reframed Abstract Expressionist canvases as arenas in which the artist performs an existential act rather than producing pictures.
Abstract Expressionist painters such as Pollock can be understood as treating the canvas less as a surface for pictorial representation and more as a stage for a recorded physical act of painting.

Michael Fried, Absorption and Theatricality: Painting and Beholder in the Age of Diderot (University of California Press, 1980), argued that eighteenth-century French painting sought to deny the beholder's presence in order to re-establish pictorial absorption.
Eighteenth-century French painting increasingly pursued the fiction of absorbed figures oblivious to the viewer, treating this denial of the beholder as a condition of serious pictorial art.
Nikolaus Pevsner, Pioneers of the Modern Movement from William Morris to Walter Gropius (Faber, 1936), narrated a teleological history of modern architecture culminating in the Bauhaus.
An influential narrative of modern architecture presents its emergence as a development running from the Arts and Crafts movement through engineering advances to the Bauhaus under Gropius.

Robert Venturi, Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture (Museum of Modern Art, 1966), argued against the reductive purity of orthodox modernism in favour of an architecture of 'both-and' rather than 'either-or'.
A major strand of late twentieth-century architectural thought rejected the purism of orthodox modernism and advocated buildings that embrace ambiguity, historical reference, and contradiction.

Jane Jacobs, The Death and Life of Great American Cities (Random House, 1961), argued that vibrant urban life depends on dense, mixed-use neighbourhoods with short blocks, aged buildings, and street-level eyes.
Lively and safe urban neighbourhoods tend to feature a mix of uses, short blocks, a range of building ages, and enough density to keep eyes on the street throughout the day.

Adolf Loos, 'Ornament und Verbrechen' (lecture 1910; published in Les Cahiers d'aujourd'hui, 1913), argued that the cultural evolution of civilized peoples is marked by the removal of ornament from everyday objects.
A central early-modernist argument held that the progress of design in industrial societies would be reflected in the elimination of unnecessary decoration from everyday objects and buildings.

Gunther Schuller, Early Jazz: Its Roots and Musical Development (Oxford University Press, 1968), analyzed the musical innovations of Louis Armstrong and his contemporaries through detailed transcription and formal analysis.
Louis Armstrong's recordings of the late 1920s introduced rhythmic and melodic innovations that transformed jazz from a collective ensemble style into a soloist-led art form.

Susan McClary, Feminine Endings: Music, Gender, and Sexuality (University of Minnesota Press, 1991), argued that Western tonal music encodes gendered narratives through cadential structures and thematic oppositions.

Western tonal music since the seventeenth century often codes its thematic and cadential structures along gendered lines, associating stability with masculine and disruptive otherness with feminine themes.

Richard Taruskin, Stravinsky and the Russian Traditions (University of California Press, 1996), situated Stravinsky's neoprimitivist works in The Rite of Spring within Russian folk and liturgical sources.
Stravinsky's early ballets, including The Rite of Spring, draw extensively on Russian folk melodies and ritual traditions, rather than being a break with tradition in favour of pure modernism.
Leonard B. Meyer, Emotion and Meaning in Music (University of Chicago Press, 1956), argued that musical affect arises from the confirmation and violation of learned stylistic expectations.
Listeners experience musical emotion largely through the way a piece plays with their learned expectations, fulfilling or frustrating implications built up by stylistic conventions.
Fred Lerdahl and Ray Jackendoff, A Generative Theory of Tonal Music (MIT Press, 1983), proposed a formal grammar of grouping, metre, time-span reduction, and prolongational reduction for tonal music.
The hierarchical structure of Western tonal music can be modelled by rule systems that segment pieces into groups, impose metrical structure, and derive tree-shaped reductions of pitch content.
Heinrich Schenker, Der freie Satz (Universal Edition, 1935), presented the Ursatz and concept of structural levels as the foundation of his theory of tonal music.
Tonal compositions of the common-practice era can be heard as elaborations of a small number of underlying voice-leading structures that prolong tonic-dominant-tonic motion across an entire work.

Sergei Eisenstein, 'A Dialectic Approach to Film Form' (1929), collected in Film Form, trans. Leyda (Harcourt, 1949), theorized montage as the collision of conflicting shots to generate new meaning dialectically.
A classical Soviet theory of montage treats film editing as the dialectical collision of shots, whose juxtaposition generates meanings not present in either shot alone.

Gilles Deleuze, Cinema 2: The Time-Image (French ed. Minuit, 1985; English trans. University of Minnesota Press, 1989), argued that postwar European cinema produces direct presentations of time rather than sensorimotor action.
Postwar European art cinema developed forms in which time is presented directly through duration and memory, rather than indirectly through goal-oriented action.

Pascale Casanova, The World Republic of Letters (French ed. Seuil, 1999; English trans. Harvard University Press, 2004), described a stratified international literary space with dominant and peripheral centres of consecration.

The global circulation of literature operates through a hierarchical system in which a few metropolitan cities act as dominant centres of consecration, while most national literatures occupy peripheral positions.

Franco Moretti, 'Conjectures on World Literature', New Left Review 1 (2000) 54-68, proposed 'distant reading' as a mode of literary analysis that treats systems rather than individual texts as primary objects.
One response to the sheer scale of world literature is to replace close reading of individual canonical works with comparative study of large-scale patterns across genres, languages, and markets.

Lawrence Venuti, The Translator's Invisibility: A History of Translation (Routledge, 1995), criticized Anglo-American norms of fluent, domesticating translation for rendering the translator invisible.
The dominant English-language tradition of fluent, idiomatic translation tends to efface the translator's role and to assimilate foreign texts to target-language stylistic norms.
Gideon Toury, Descriptive Translation Studies and Beyond (John Benjamins, 1995), argued that translations should be studied as facts of their target culture, governed by translational norms.
Translations can be analyzed empirically as products shaped by the literary and social norms of the culture that receives them, rather than evaluated only against the source text.

Stuart Hall, 'Encoding/Decoding' (1973; published in Culture, Media, Language, Hutchinson, 1980), argued that audiences may adopt dominant, negotiated, or oppositional readings of a televisual message.
A single televisual message does not uniquely determine its reception; audiences can accept its preferred meaning, modify it, or read it against the grain depending on their social position.
Raymond Williams, Marxism and Literature (Oxford University Press, 1977), developed the concept of 'structures of feeling' to capture emergent experiences not yet codified in dominant ideology.
Cultures at any given moment contain emergent patterns of shared experience that have not yet hardened into explicit ideology, and literature often registers these structures of feeling first.

Theodor W. Adorno and Max Horkheimer, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception', in Dialectic of Enlightenment (Querido, 1947), argued that industrially produced culture standardizes taste and blocks critical reflection.
Industrially produced mass entertainment tends to standardize cultural products and the responses they elicit, working against the autonomous, critical reception associated with older notions of art.
John Dewey, Art as Experience (Minton, Balch & Co., 1934), argued that aesthetic experience is continuous with ordinary experience intensified and unified, not a separate metaphysical realm.
Aesthetic experience is not sealed off from the rest of life but arises when ordinary perceptual and practical activity is intensified, unified, and felt as a coherent whole.
Arthur C. Danto, 'The Artworld', Journal of Philosophy 61 (1964) 571-584, argued that something becomes an artwork only against a theoretical atmosphere and history of art — the artworld.
Whether a given object counts as a work of art depends not on its perceptible properties alone but on its position within a historically situated network of theories, institutions, and practices.

Heinrich Woelfflin, Principles of Art History (German ed. 1915; English trans. Dover, 1932), proposed five polar pairs — linear vs painterly, plane vs recession, closed vs open form, multiplicity vs unity, absolute vs relative clarity — to characterize the shift from Renaissance to Baroque.

The stylistic shift from Renaissance to Baroque visual art can be described through a series of formal polarities contrasting linear clarity and stable composition with painterly fluidity and dynamic recession.

Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick, Epistemology of the Closet (University of California Press, 1990), argued that much of modern Western thought is structured by a crisis of homo/heterosexual definition since the late nineteenth century.

A wide range of modern Western categories — including those in literature, law, and psychology — have been shaped by the unstable opposition between homosexual and heterosexual definitions that crystallized in the late nineteenth century.

W. J. T. Mitchell, 'The Pictorial Turn', Picture Theory (University of Chicago Press, 1994), argued that late twentieth-century thought had undergone a shift from the linguistic turn to a renewed interest in images and visuality.
Late twentieth-century humanistic inquiry increasingly turned from language-centred models of meaning toward the study of images, visuality, and their role in structuring knowledge and power.

Joseph Kerman, 'How We Got into Analysis, and How to Get Out', Critical Inquiry 7 (1980) 311-331, argued that Anglo-American musicology had over-invested in positivist analysis at the expense of critical and hermeneutic engagement.
Late twentieth-century musicology was criticized for focusing too narrowly on formal and analytic description of scores at the expense of interpretive, historical, and critical engagement with music.

Victor Papanek, Design for the Real World: Human Ecology and Social Change (Pantheon, 1971), argued that industrial design had become complicit in producing wasteful, socially harmful products and should be reoriented toward real human and ecological needs.

A long-running strand of design thought holds that industrial design has often served consumer markets in wasteful and ecologically damaging ways and should be refocused on genuine human and environmental needs.

Adrian Forty, Words and Buildings: A Vocabulary of Modern Architecture (Thames & Hudson, 2000), traced the historical transformation of key terms such as 'space', 'form', 'function', 'design', and 'structure' within modern architectural discourse.
Core vocabulary of modern architecture such as 'space', 'form', and 'function' carries a layered history in which each term's meaning has shifted substantially since the nineteenth century.

E. H. Gombrich, Art and Illusion (Bollingen / Princeton University Press, 1960), argued that pictorial representation develops through schemata and correction, with artists always mediating perception through inherited conventions.
Pictorial representation is never a direct copy of nature but always proceeds through inherited schemata that artists modify, so every era's 'realism' is conditioned by conventions of depiction.

George Steiner, After Babel: Aspects of Language and Translation (Oxford University Press, 1975), argued that understanding even within a single language is a form of translation, and that translation is a fourfold hermeneutic movement.
Understanding any utterance involves an act of translation, and translation between languages can be analyzed as a hermeneutic process of trust, aggression, incorporation, and restitution.

W. K. Wimsatt and Monroe Beardsley, 'The Intentional Fallacy', Sewanee Review 54 (1946) 468-488, argued that the author's intention is neither available nor desirable as a standard for judging the success of a literary work.

One influential position in twentieth-century literary criticism holds that the meaning and value of a literary work should be assessed from the text itself rather than from claims about the author's private intentions.
IPCC AR6 Working Group I Summary for Policymakers (2021), statement A.1.2, reports that global surface temperature increased by 1.09 degrees Celsius in 2011 to 2020 relative to 1850 to 1900.
Global mean surface temperature in the 2011 to 2020 decade was about 1.1 degrees Celsius higher than the 1850 to 1900 pre-industrial baseline.
IPCC AR6 WGI Summary for Policymakers (2021), statement A.1, concludes that it is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean, and land.
Human activities are the dominant cause of observed warming of the atmosphere, ocean, and land since the mid-twentieth century.
NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory data from the Mauna Loa Observatory reported a 2023 annual mean atmospheric CO2 mole fraction of 421.1 parts per million, the highest in the instrumental record.
The annual mean atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration at Mauna Loa reached about 421 parts per million in 2023, the highest level ever directly measured.
Luthi et al., Nature 453 (2008) 379-382, extended the EPICA Dome C ice core CO2 record to 800,000 years and showed atmospheric CO2 stayed between 172 and 300 parts per million across that interval.
Ice core records show that atmospheric carbon dioxide remained between roughly 170 and 300 parts per million throughout the past 800,000 years, well below present levels.

Cheng et al., Advances in Atmospheric Sciences 40 (2023) 963-974, reported that global ocean heat content in the upper 2000 metres reached a new record in 2022, with 2022 exceeding 2021 by 10.9 zettajoules.
The heat content of the upper 2000 metres of the global ocean reached a new record high in 2022, continuing a multi-decadal warming trend.
IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 5 (2021) assesses that the surface open ocean pH has declined by approximately 0.017 to 0.027 units per decade since the late 1980s due to uptake of anthropogenic CO2.
Uptake of human-emitted carbon dioxide has lowered surface ocean pH by roughly 0.02 units per decade since the 1980s, a process known as ocean acidification.
NSIDC Sea Ice Index v3 records show the September Arctic sea ice extent has declined at about 12.6 percent per decade relative to the 1981 to 2010 mean.
September Arctic sea ice extent has been shrinking at roughly 13 percent per decade relative to the late twentieth century average.

The IMBIE Team, Nature 579 (2020) 233-239, estimated that the Greenland Ice Sheet lost 3902 plus-or-minus 342 gigatonnes of ice between 1992 and 2018, contributing 10.8 millimetres to global sea level.
The Greenland Ice Sheet lost nearly 4000 gigatonnes of mass between 1992 and 2018, raising global mean sea level by about 11 millimetres.
The IMBIE Team, Nature 558 (2018) 219-222, reported that the Antarctic Ice Sheet lost 2720 plus-or-minus 1390 gigatonnes between 1992 and 2017, with accelerating losses from West Antarctica.
The Antarctic Ice Sheet has lost mass since 1992 with an accelerating trend driven primarily by ice shelf thinning and glacier retreat in West Antarctica.
IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 9 (2021) assesses that global mean sea level rose by 0.20 metres between 1901 and 2018 and that the rate accelerated to 3.7 millimetres per year during 2006 to 2018.
Global mean sea level rose about 20 centimetres between 1901 and 2018, with the rate accelerating to nearly 4 millimetres per year after 2006.

Article 2 of the Paris Agreement (UNFCCC, 2015) sets the long-term goal of holding the increase in global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit warming to 1.5 degrees.
Parties to the Paris Agreement committed to holding global warming well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees.

The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer (UNEP, 1987) mandated the phased elimination of chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting substances, with subsequent amendments including the 2016 Kigali Amendment on hydrofluorocarbons.
An international treaty phased out chlorofluorocarbons and related ozone-depleting substances, later extended to cover hydrofluorocarbons, which are potent greenhouse gases.
WMO Scientific Assessment of Ozone Depletion 2022 projects that Antarctic springtime ozone will return to 1980 values around 2066 if current compliance with the Montreal Protocol continues.
Antarctic springtime stratospheric ozone is projected to recover to its 1980 values around the mid-2060s if nations continue to comply with the existing ozone-protection treaty.
IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 5 Table 5.8 (2021) estimates the remaining carbon budget from the start of 2020 for a 50 percent chance of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees at 500 gigatonnes of CO2.
The remaining budget of carbon dioxide emissions consistent with a 50 percent chance of staying under 1.5 degrees of warming was about 500 gigatonnes as of the start of 2020.

Friedlingstein et al., 'Global Carbon Budget 2023', Earth System Science Data 15 (2023) 5301-5369, report that fossil CO2 emissions reached 36.8 gigatonnes in 2022 and constitute about 90 percent of total anthropogenic CO2 emissions.
Fossil fuel combustion and industrial processes released about 37 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide in 2022 and account for roughly 90 percent of all human-caused CO2 emissions.
Friedlingstein et al., 'Global Carbon Budget 2023', ESSD 15 (2023) 5301-5369, estimate that land and ocean sinks together absorbed about 54 percent of anthropogenic CO2 emissions over 2013 to 2022.
Natural land and ocean sinks together remove roughly half of human-emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere each year, slowing the build-up of atmospheric CO2.
Hansen et al., Science 342 (2013) 850-853, mapped global forest cover change at 30 metre resolution and estimated a gross loss of 2.3 million square kilometres of tree cover between 2000 and 2012.
Roughly 2.3 million square kilometres of tree cover were lost worldwide between 2000 and 2012, with hotspots concentrated in the tropics.
Gatti et al., Nature 595 (2021) 388-393, used aircraft observations to show that the southeastern Amazon has become a net source of atmospheric CO2, driven by deforestation and climate warming.
Parts of the southeastern Amazon rainforest have switched from net carbon sink to net source in recent years, largely due to deforestation and warming.

Hughes et al., Nature 543 (2017) 373-377, documented mass bleaching of the Great Barrier Reef in 2016, with 91 percent of surveyed reefs showing bleaching and strong correlation with degree-heating-weeks.
A 2016 marine heatwave triggered widespread coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef, affecting more than 90 percent of the reefs that were surveyed.
IPBES Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (2019) estimates that around one million animal and plant species are threatened with extinction, many within decades.
Roughly one million animal and plant species are currently at risk of extinction, many within the coming decades, according to global biodiversity assessments.
Hallmann et al., PLOS ONE 12 (2017) e0185809, reported a 76 percent decline in total flying insect biomass in German protected areas over 27 years of Malaise-trap sampling.
Long-term monitoring in German nature reserves recorded a decline of roughly three-quarters in flying insect biomass over 27 years.
Oliver et al., Nature Communications 9 (2018) 1324, analysed satellite records and reported that marine heatwave days increased by 54 percent globally between 1925 and 2016.
The number of marine heatwave days worldwide has risen by more than half over the past century as the ocean surface has warmed.
Kossin et al., PNAS 117 (2020) 11975-11980, found a global increase in the probability of major tropical cyclone intensity of about 8 percent per decade over 1979 to 2017 in satellite-derived data.
The share of tropical cyclones reaching major hurricane intensity has increased by roughly 8 percent per decade since 1979.

Philip et al., Earth System Dynamics 13 (2022) 1689-1713, attributed the 2022 western European heatwave to human-induced climate change, concluding such events are now about ten times more likely than in a pre-industrial climate.
Heatwaves as severe as the 2022 western European event are now roughly ten times more likely than they would have been without human-caused climate change.

IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 11 (2021) assesses that heavy precipitation events over most land areas have intensified at a rate broadly consistent with the Clausius-Clapeyron scaling of about 7 percent per degree of warming.
Heavy precipitation events over most land areas have become more intense, with atmospheric water vapour capacity increasing by roughly 7 percent for each degree of warming.

Williams et al., Nature Climate Change 12 (2022) 232-234, concluded that the 2000 to 2021 drought in southwestern North America was the driest 22-year period in at least 1200 years as reconstructed from tree rings.
The 2000 to 2021 drought in southwestern North America was the driest 22-year span in the region in at least twelve centuries.
Caesar et al., Nature Geoscience 14 (2021) 118-120, reconstructed the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation from proxies and reported that it is at its weakest in more than a millennium.
The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is now weaker than at any point in the past thousand years, based on multi-proxy reconstructions.
Schuur et al., Nature 520 (2015) 171-179, estimated that northern permafrost soils contain about 1460 to 1600 petagrams of organic carbon, nearly twice the current atmospheric carbon pool.
Northern permafrost soils store roughly 1500 petagrams of organic carbon, almost double the amount currently in the atmosphere.
NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory data show that globally averaged atmospheric methane increased by 18.0 parts per billion in 2021, the largest annual growth in the modern record beginning in 1983.
Atmospheric methane grew by 18 parts per billion in 2021, the largest one-year increase observed since systematic global measurements began in 1983.
Solomon et al., Science 327 (2010) 1219-1223, showed that a decline in stratospheric water vapour after 2000 slowed the rate of surface warming by about 25 percent relative to the preceding decade.
A post-2000 decline in stratospheric water vapour temporarily reduced the rate of global surface warming compared with the 1990s.

Bellouin et al., Reviews of Geophysics 58 (2020) e2019RG000660, assessed the effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions as minus 1.0 watts per square metre with a range from minus 1.7 to minus 0.3.
Aerosol-cloud interactions exert a net cooling influence on Earth's energy balance of roughly one watt per square metre, partially offsetting greenhouse warming.

The WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines 2021 lowered the annual mean PM2.5 guideline to 5 micrograms per cubic metre, citing cumulative evidence that ambient fine particle pollution causes millions of premature deaths annually.

The World Health Organization sets the annual safe limit for fine particulate matter at 5 micrograms per cubic metre; exposure above this level causes millions of premature deaths worldwide each year.
EPA Integrated Science Assessment for Ozone and Related Photochemical Oxidants (EPA/600/R-20/012, 2020) concludes that short-term ozone exposure causes respiratory morbidity and premature mortality.
Short-term exposure to ground-level ozone increases respiratory illness and premature mortality, particularly in vulnerable populations.

IRENA, 'Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2022' (2023), reports the global weighted-average levelised cost of electricity from utility-scale solar photovoltaics fell from USD 0.445 per kilowatt-hour in 2010 to USD 0.049 per kilowatt-hour in 2022.
The global average cost of electricity from utility-scale solar photovoltaics dropped roughly ninefold between 2010 and 2022, falling below five US cents per kilowatt-hour.
IRENA, 'Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2022' (2023), reports that the global weighted-average LCOE of onshore wind fell from USD 0.107 per kWh in 2010 to USD 0.033 per kWh in 2022.
The global average cost of onshore wind electricity has fallen by nearly 70 percent since 2010 to around three US cents per kilowatt-hour.
IEA, 'Global EV Outlook 2023', reports that electric car sales reached 10 million in 2022, raising their share of new car sales to 14 percent globally.
Electric cars accounted for about 14 percent of new passenger car sales worldwide in 2022, with total annual sales reaching 10 million units.
The Glasgow Climate Pact, adopted at UNFCCC COP26 in 2021, calls on parties to accelerate efforts toward the phase-down of unabated coal power and phase-out of inefficient fossil-fuel subsidies.
Parties at the 2021 UN climate summit agreed to accelerate the phase-down of unabated coal power and phase out inefficient fossil-fuel subsidies.

IEA, 'CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions' (2023), reports that around 45 commercial facilities capture about 45 million tonnes of CO2 per year globally, well below the scale envisaged in net-zero scenarios.
Operating carbon-capture facilities worldwide remove around 45 million tonnes of CO2 per year, a small fraction of what net-zero scenarios require.

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, 'Reflecting Sunlight' (2021), recommends a cautious, federally coordinated research programme on solar geoengineering while emphasising that it is not a substitute for emissions reduction.
Expert panels recommend cautious, government-coordinated research on solar geoengineering while stressing that it cannot substitute for cutting greenhouse-gas emissions.

Tilmes et al., JGR Atmospheres 123 (2018) 4616-4641, used CESM1 simulations to show that stratospheric aerosol injection could offset tropospheric warming but would alter regional precipitation and monsoon circulations.
Model studies indicate stratospheric aerosol injection could partially offset surface warming, but would also disrupt regional precipitation patterns and monsoon systems.
WRI Aqueduct 4.0 (2023) estimates that 25 countries, home to a quarter of the world's population, face extremely high water stress, with withdrawals exceeding 80 percent of renewable supply.
About a quarter of the world's population lives in 25 countries where water withdrawals exceed 80 percent of renewable supply, classified as extremely high water stress.

Hugonnet et al., Nature 592 (2021) 726-731, used satellite stereo imagery to estimate that glaciers outside the ice sheets lost 267 gigatonnes per year between 2000 and 2019, contributing 0.74 millimetres per year to sea level rise.
Mountain glaciers outside the great ice sheets lost mass at about 267 gigatonnes per year over 2000 to 2019, adding roughly 0.7 millimetres per year to global sea level.

Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service press release (2023) reported that Canadian wildfires released about 480 megatonnes of carbon in 2023, more than double the previous annual record for the country.
The 2023 Canadian wildfire season released roughly 480 megatonnes of carbon, more than double any previous year on record for the country.

The European Commission Joint Research Centre report, 'Drought in Europe August 2022' (JRC130738, 2022), concluded that 47 percent of the territory of the European Union was under drought warning conditions in August 2022, the worst in at least 500 years.
Nearly half of the European Union faced drought warning conditions in August 2022, making it the continent's worst drought in at least five centuries.
Donato et al., Nature Geoscience 4 (2011) 293-297, showed that mangroves store 1023 megagrams of carbon per hectare on average, among the most carbon-rich forests in the tropics.
Mangrove forests store on the order of 1000 tonnes of carbon per hectare, making them one of the most carbon-dense ecosystems in the tropics.
Rockstrom et al., Nature 461 (2009) 472-475, identified the anthropogenic nitrogen fixation rate of about 121 teragrams per year as exceeding the proposed planetary boundary of 35 teragrams per year.
Humans fix reactive nitrogen at roughly three times the rate considered safe for ecosystems, driving widespread eutrophication and pollution of waterways.

Rignot et al., Science 341 (2013) 266-270, used satellite data to estimate that Antarctic ice-shelf basal melting accounts for 1325 gigatonnes per year, exceeding iceberg calving as the main mass-loss process.
Basal melting beneath Antarctic ice shelves now removes more ice per year than iceberg calving, with a combined loss of over 1300 gigatonnes annually.

Pistone, Eisenman, and Ramanathan, PNAS 111 (2014) 3322-3326, used CERES satellite data to estimate that loss of Arctic sea ice from 1979 to 2011 caused a globally averaged radiative forcing of 0.21 watts per square metre.
Loss of reflective Arctic sea ice since 1979 has added about 0.2 watts per square metre to Earth's energy imbalance, amplifying greenhouse-gas warming.

NOAA Climate Prediction Center diagnostics and the ECMWF SEAS5 seasonal forecasts indicated in mid-2023 that a strong El Nino event had developed in the tropical Pacific, consistent with widespread warm and dry anomalies across many regions.
A strong El Nino event developed in the tropical Pacific during 2023, driving warm and dry anomalies across many regions of the world.

The Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC (1997), Annex B, set binding quantified emission-limitation commitments for industrialised countries, averaging a 5 percent reduction below 1990 levels over 2008 to 2012.
The Kyoto Protocol bound industrialised countries to reduce their greenhouse-gas emissions by an average of 5 percent below 1990 levels during 2008 to 2012.

Stanley Milgram, 'Behavioral Study of Obedience', Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 67 (1963) 371-378, reported that 65 percent of adult participants continued to deliver what they believed were increasingly severe electric shocks to a confederate at the instruction of an experimenter.
Under direct instruction from a perceived authority figure, a large majority of ordinary adults are willing to administer what they believe are dangerous electric shocks to another person.

Bandura, Ross, and Ross, 'Transmission of Aggression through Imitation of Aggressive Models', Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 63 (1961) 575-582, showed that children who observed an adult model attack a Bobo doll later reproduced the same aggressive behaviour more often than control children.
Young children who watch adults behave aggressively toward an inflatable doll are substantially more likely to imitate that aggression themselves when given the opportunity.

Baumeister and Leary, 'The Need to Belong: Desire for Interpersonal Attachments as a Fundamental Human Motivation', Psychological Bulletin 117 (1995) 497-529, argued that the need for stable, caring social bonds is a pervasive and fundamental human motive with broad cognitive, emotional, and health consequences.
The drive to form and maintain lasting interpersonal bonds is a basic human motivation, and persistent failure to satisfy it is linked to poorer mental and physical health outcomes.

Tversky and Kahneman, 'Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases', Science 185 (1974) 1124-1131, described how people rely on a small number of cognitive heuristics - representativeness, availability, and anchoring - that produce systematic deviations from normative probability judgments.

When estimating probabilities people rely on mental shortcuts such as how typical an example seems, how easily instances come to mind, and whichever number was suggested first, leading to predictable biases.

Kahneman and Tversky, 'Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk', Econometrica 47 (1979) 263-292, introduced a model in which people evaluate outcomes as gains or losses from a reference point and are roughly twice as sensitive to losses as to equivalent gains.
People evaluate risky outcomes relative to a reference point rather than in terms of final wealth, and a loss of a given size generally feels about twice as intense as a gain of the same size.

Solomon Asch, 'Studies of Independence and Conformity: A Minority of One Against a Unanimous Majority', Psychological Monographs 70 (1956), reported that about one-third of participants conformed to a unanimous but clearly incorrect group judgment on a simple line-matching task.
When a unanimous group gives an obviously wrong answer on a simple perceptual task, a substantial fraction of individuals will publicly agree with the group rather than report what they actually see.

Festinger and Carlsmith, 'Cognitive Consequences of Forced Compliance', Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 58 (1959) 203-210, found that participants paid only one dollar to describe a boring task as enjoyable later rated the task more favorably than those paid twenty dollars.
People who are induced to publicly endorse a position for a small reward later come to hold that position more sincerely than people paid a large reward for the same endorsement.

Haney, Banks, and Zimbardo, 'Interpersonal Dynamics in a Simulated Prison', International Journal of Criminology and Penology 1 (1973) 69-97, reported that college students randomly assigned to guard and prisoner roles rapidly adopted abusive and submissive behaviour, forcing early termination of the study.
Assigning ordinary people to strong social roles such as guard and prisoner in a simulated institution can rapidly produce coercive behaviour on one side and submission on the other.

David Rosenhan, 'On Being Sane in Insane Places', Science 179 (1973) 250-258, described how pseudopatients who briefly feigned a single symptom were admitted to psychiatric hospitals and then diagnosed as mentally ill despite subsequently behaving normally.
Once people are labelled as psychiatric patients, staff in mental hospitals tend to reinterpret their normal behaviour through the lens of the diagnosis and have difficulty recognising them as sane.

Ainsworth, Blehar, Waters, and Wall, Patterns of Attachment (Lawrence Erlbaum, 1978), introduced the Strange Situation procedure and classified infant-caregiver attachment as secure, anxious-resistant, or anxious-avoidant.
Infants' responses to brief separation from and reunion with a caregiver fall into recognisable attachment patterns, including secure, anxious-resistant, and anxious-avoidant styles.

Jean Piaget, The Child's Conception of Number (Routledge and Kegan Paul, 1952), documented that children below about seven years typically fail conservation-of-number tasks in which physical rearrangement changes perceived quantity.
Young children under roughly seven years of age often judge that the number of objects has changed when the objects are simply spread out or rearranged in space.

Harry Harlow, 'The Nature of Love', American Psychologist 13 (1958) 673-685, reported that infant rhesus monkeys strongly preferred a cloth surrogate mother that provided contact comfort over a wire surrogate that provided food.
Infant monkeys separated from their mothers prefer a soft cloth-covered surrogate that offers contact comfort over a wire surrogate that only provides food.

Seligman and Maier, 'Failure to Escape Traumatic Shock', Journal of Experimental Psychology 74 (1967) 1-9, showed that dogs exposed to inescapable shock later failed to escape or avoid shocks they could control, a phenomenon termed learned helplessness.
Animals and humans repeatedly exposed to aversive events they cannot control tend to stop trying to escape such events even when escape later becomes possible.

Aaron Beck, 'Thinking and Depression: Idiosyncratic Content and Cognitive Distortions', Archives of General Psychiatry 9 (1963) 324-333, proposed that depression is maintained by systematic negative distortions in automatic thoughts about the self, the world, and the future.
Depression is sustained in part by systematic negative biases in how people think about themselves, their circumstances, and their future prospects.

Costa and McCrae, 'Four Ways Five Factors are Basic', Personality and Individual Differences 13 (1992) 653-665, consolidated evidence that personality variation in adults is well described by five broad dimensions: openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.
Individual differences in adult personality are largely captured by five broad trait dimensions commonly labelled openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.

Mischel, Shoda, and Rodriguez, 'Delay of Gratification in Children', Science 244 (1989) 933-938, summarized longitudinal follow-ups of preschool children who waited longer in the marshmallow paradigm and later showed better adolescent cognitive and social competence.
Preschool children who can wait longer for a larger delayed reward tend on average to show somewhat better cognitive and social outcomes in adolescence.

Carol Dweck, Mindset: The New Psychology of Success (Random House, 2006), synthesized research showing that students who believe intelligence is malleable tend to seek challenge and persist after failure more than those who view intelligence as fixed.
Students who believe that intelligence can grow with effort tend to embrace challenging work and recover from setbacks better than students who see intelligence as an unchangeable trait.

Thaler and Sunstein, Nudge: Improving Decisions about Health, Wealth, and Happiness (Yale University Press, 2008), argued that small changes in choice architecture, such as default options, can predictably alter behaviour without restricting freedom of choice.

Changing the default option in a decision, such as whether employees are automatically enrolled in a savings plan, can substantially shift participation rates without removing anyone's ability to opt out.

Mazar, Amir, and Ariely, 'The Dishonesty of Honest People: A Theory of Self-Concept Maintenance', Journal of Marketing Research 45 (2008) 633-644, reported that many participants cheat by small amounts on anonymous tasks but refrain from large cheating that would threaten their self-image as honest.

When given an opportunity to cheat without detection, many otherwise honest people cheat by small amounts but stop short of cheating enough to seriously threaten their view of themselves as good people.

Klein et al., 'Investigating Variation in Replicability: A Many Labs Replication Project', Social Psychology 45 (2014) 142-152, coordinated 36 independent labs to replicate 13 classic findings and found that roughly ten of the effects reproduced while others did not.
Large coordinated replication efforts have shown that many but not all classic social psychology findings reliably reproduce across samples and laboratories.

Open Science Collaboration, 'Estimating the Reproducibility of Psychological Science', Science 349 (2015) aac4716, replicated 100 published psychology studies and found that only about 36 percent yielded statistically significant results in the same direction.
In a large replication project covering a hundred published psychology studies, only a little over a third reproduced the original statistically significant finding.

Roethlisberger and Dickson, Management and the Worker (Harvard University Press, 1939), reported that female assembly workers at the Hawthorne Works showed productivity gains that appeared tied to being observed rather than to specific lighting or break manipulations.
Workers whose behaviour is being observed as part of a study may increase their productivity simply because they know they are being watched, regardless of the specific conditions being tested.

Frederick Herzberg, 'One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?', Harvard Business Review 46 (1968) 53-62, distinguished hygiene factors such as pay and supervision from motivators such as achievement and recognition that drive satisfaction.
In workplaces, factors like pay and working conditions mainly prevent dissatisfaction, while genuine motivation tends to come from achievement, recognition, and meaningful work.

Hackman and Oldham, 'Motivation through the Design of Work: Test of a Theory', Organizational Behavior and Human Performance 16 (1976) 250-279, proposed that five core job characteristics - skill variety, task identity, task significance, autonomy, and feedback - shape intrinsic motivation.
Jobs that combine varied skills, a clear whole task, meaningful impact, autonomy, and regular feedback tend to produce higher intrinsic motivation in workers.

McDaniel, Whetzel, Schmidt, and Maurer, 'The Validity of Employment Interviews: A Comprehensive Review and Meta-Analysis', Journal of Applied Psychology 79 (1994) 599-616, reported that structured interviews predict job performance substantially better than unstructured interviews.
Structured employment interviews with standardised questions and scoring rubrics predict later job performance much more accurately than free-form unstructured interviews.

James S. Coleman, Equality of Educational Opportunity (U.S. Government Printing Office, 1966), concluded from a survey of over 600,000 American students that family background accounted for more variance in student achievement than measurable school resources.
In large-scale surveys of American schoolchildren, differences in family socioeconomic background account for more of the variation in academic achievement than differences in school resources.

Christopher Jencks et al., Inequality: A Reassessment of the Effect of Family and Schooling in America (Basic Books, 1972), argued that equalizing school quality would produce only modest reductions in overall income inequality.
Equalising school resources across neighbourhoods would likely produce only modest reductions in overall adult income inequality because many other factors drive earnings differences.

Pierre Bourdieu, 'Cultural Reproduction and Social Reproduction' in Knowledge, Education and Cultural Change (ed. Brown, 1973), argued that schools reward a cultural capital unevenly distributed by class, reproducing social hierarchy across generations.
Schools tend to reward tastes, language, and knowledge that are more common in middle- and upper-class homes, which helps reproduce class advantages across generations.

Mark Granovetter, 'The Strength of Weak Ties', American Journal of Sociology 78 (1973) 1360-1380, reported that professional and technical workers in the Boston area who found new jobs typically did so through acquaintances rather than through close friends.
People looking for jobs more often find useful leads through weak social ties such as acquaintances than through their closest friends, because weak ties connect to different information networks.

Mark Granovetter, 'Economic Action and Social Structure: The Problem of Embeddedness', American Journal of Sociology 91 (1985) 481-510, argued that economic transactions are persistently embedded in ongoing networks of interpersonal relations rather than occurring among atomized actors.
Economic exchanges are consistently shaped by the ongoing personal relationships and social networks in which the parties are embedded, not by isolated self-interested calculation alone.

Brian Uzzi, 'Social Structure and Competition in Interfirm Networks: The Paradox of Embeddedness', Administrative Science Quarterly 42 (1997) 35-67, showed that New York garment firms that relied on a mix of arm's-length and embedded ties outperformed those using only one type of tie.
Firms tend to perform best when their supply relationships combine close, trust-based ties with a broader set of more transactional relationships rather than relying on only one mode.

Robert Putnam, Making Democracy Work: Civic Traditions in Modern Italy (Princeton University Press, 1993), found that regions with denser horizontal civic associations had more effective regional governments than regions with sparser civic life.
Regions with stronger traditions of voluntary civic participation tend to have more effective and responsive local government than regions with weaker associational life.

Robert Putnam, Bowling Alone: The Collapse and Revival of American Community (Simon and Schuster, 2000), documented long-run declines in membership in civic, religious, and voluntary associations across the United States during the second half of the twentieth century.
Participation in American civic, religious, and voluntary associations declined substantially over the second half of the twentieth century.

William Julius Wilson, The Truly Disadvantaged (University of Chicago Press, 1987), argued that deindustrialization and middle-class outmigration left concentrated urban black neighborhoods with high joblessness and social isolation.
The collapse of manufacturing employment and the departure of middle-class residents from many American inner-city neighborhoods left behind concentrated poverty and social isolation.

Massey and Denton, American Apartheid: Segregation and the Making of the Underclass (Harvard University Press, 1993), used census tract data to show that black Americans faced unusually high and persistent levels of residential segregation compared with other groups.
Black Americans have faced unusually high and persistent levels of residential segregation in U.S. metropolitan areas compared with other racial and ethnic groups.

Chetty, Hendren, Kline, and Saez, 'Where is the Land of Opportunity? The Geography of Intergenerational Mobility in the United States', Quarterly Journal of Economics 129 (2014) 1553-1623, used tax records for 40 million children and their parents to document large regional differences in upward mobility.

Upward economic mobility varies dramatically across U.S. regions, with some metropolitan areas offering much better chances for children from low-income families to reach higher income brackets than others.

Samuel Preston, 'The Changing Relation between Mortality and Level of Economic Development', Population Studies 29 (1975) 231-248, showed that life expectancy at a given income level rose substantially during the twentieth century, implying that factors beyond income drove mortality decline.
Life expectancy rose at every level of income over the twentieth century, indicating that much of the long-run decline in mortality was driven by factors beyond rising income.

Frank Notestein, 'Population: The Long View' in Food for the World (ed. Schultz, 1945), articulated the demographic transition theory in which mortality declines precede fertility declines during modernization.
During modernization, societies typically experience a fall in death rates before birth rates drop, producing a period of rapid population growth followed by stabilisation at lower vital rates.

Sampson, Raudenbush, and Earls, 'Neighborhoods and Violent Crime: A Multilevel Study of Collective Efficacy', Science 277 (1997) 918-924, found that neighborhood collective efficacy predicted lower rates of violence in Chicago even after controlling for concentrated disadvantage.
Neighborhoods where residents trust one another and are willing to intervene for the common good tend to have lower rates of violent crime, even after accounting for poverty and other disadvantage.

Cohen and Felson, 'Social Change and Crime Rate Trends: A Routine Activity Approach', American Sociological Review 44 (1979) 588-608, argued that predatory crime requires the convergence in time and space of a motivated offender, a suitable target, and the absence of capable guardians.
Predatory crime tends to occur when a motivated offender, an attractive target, and a lack of effective guardians come together in the same time and place.

Wilson and Kelling, 'Broken Windows: The Police and Neighborhood Safety', The Atlantic (March 1982), argued that visible signs of disorder such as broken windows and graffiti signal that no one is in charge and encourage more serious crime.
Visible signs of neighborhood disorder such as broken windows, graffiti, and litter can signal a lack of social control and encourage additional and more serious criminal behaviour.

Gottfredson and Hirschi, A General Theory of Crime (Stanford University Press, 1990), proposed that low self-control, formed in childhood and stable across the life course, is the primary individual-level predictor of criminal behaviour.
Individual differences in self-control established in childhood are one of the strongest and most stable individual-level predictors of later involvement in crime.

Verba, Schlozman, and Brady, Voice and Equality: Civic Voluntarism in American Politics (Harvard University Press, 1995), showed that political participation in the United States is strongly stratified by socioeconomic resources, civic skills, and recruitment.
Political participation in the United States is strongly tilted toward citizens with higher income, education, and civic skills, and those who are more often recruited into political activity.

Philip Converse, 'The Nature of Belief Systems in Mass Publics' in Ideology and Discontent (ed. Apter, 1964), argued that most ordinary citizens have weakly structured and unstable political belief systems compared with political elites.
Most ordinary citizens hold political opinions that are far less internally consistent and stable over time than the opinions held by political elites and activists.

Stanley Milgram, 'The Small-World Problem', Psychology Today 1 (1967) 61-67, reported that chains of acquaintances connecting randomly chosen Americans to a distant target person typically contained only about five or six intermediaries.
Chains of acquaintances connecting two random people in a large population often involve only a handful of intermediaries, a pattern popularly summarised as six degrees of separation.

Watts and Strogatz, 'Collective Dynamics of Small-World Networks', Nature 393 (1998) 440-442, showed that adding a small number of long-range shortcuts to a regular lattice sharply reduces the average path length while preserving high clustering.
Many real social and biological networks combine high local clustering with short average path lengths, a pattern that can emerge when a mostly regular network contains a few long-range connections.

Christakis and Fowler, 'The Spread of Obesity in a Large Social Network over 32 Years', New England Journal of Medicine 357 (2007) 370-379, used Framingham Heart Study data to report that a person's chance of becoming obese rose when a close social contact became obese.
A person's likelihood of becoming obese tends to rise when people in their close social network also become obese, suggesting that health behaviours spread through social ties.

Robin Dunbar, 'Neocortex Size as a Constraint on Group Size in Primates', Journal of Human Evolution 22 (1992) 469-493, proposed on the basis of primate neocortex ratios that humans can maintain stable personal relationships with only about 150 other individuals.
Humans can typically sustain stable meaningful personal relationships with only about 150 other people, a ceiling that appears linked to the size of our social brain.

Ranehill et al., 'Assessing the Robustness of Power Posing: No Effect on Hormones and Risk Tolerance in a Large Sample of Men and Women', Psychological Science 26 (2015) 653-656, failed to replicate the hormonal and risk-tolerance effects of expansive postures originally reported by Carney, Cuddy, and Yap.
Large replication attempts have failed to reproduce earlier claims that briefly holding expansive body postures meaningfully changes hormone levels or risk-taking behaviour.

Hagger et al., 'A Multilab Preregistered Replication of the Ego-Depletion Effect', Perspectives on Psychological Science 11 (2016) 546-573, coordinated 23 laboratories and found essentially no evidence for the classic ego-depletion effect on subsequent self-control tasks.

A large coordinated replication project found little evidence that briefly exerting self-control measurably degrades performance on a subsequent self-control task, challenging earlier ego-depletion findings.
Switched from Next.js App Router to Astro for the marketing site after hydration costs pushed Largest Contentful Paint past 3.4 seconds on mid-tier Android devices.
Marketing pages ship as static Astro 4 islands with React islands hydrated only for the quote calculator and the search dialog, sharing a single shadcn/ui theme token bundle.
Migrated the admin dashboard from Create React App to Vite 5 after webpack cold starts crossed 70 seconds on the design team's MacBook Airs.
The admin dashboard builds with Vite 5 using SWC for transforms, esbuild for prebundling, and a vendor manualChunks split that keeps the recharts bundle outside the first-load JS.
Moved product detail pages from on-demand SSR to Incremental Static Regeneration with a 60-second revalidate after origin CPU pegged during price update storms.
Product pages render via Next.js ISR with revalidate=60, on-demand revalidation triggered by a Kafka consumer on pricing events, and a stale-while-revalidate CDN policy in front.
Chose full SSG over SSR for the developer documentation portal because the content is Git-sourced MDX and there is no per-user state to render.
Docs are pre-rendered by Astro at build time from MDX sources in the monorepo, deployed as immutable static files to Cloudflare Pages with a search index generated at build.
Replaced Redux Toolkit with Zustand in the trading console after boilerplate for every new slice slowed feature delivery and discouraged typed selectors.
Trading console state is split into five Zustand stores (orders, portfolio, market data, UI, session) each with its own persist middleware and immer middleware for nested updates.
Adopted Jotai over a tree of React Contexts for the form-heavy onboarding flow after nested providers forced full-tree rerenders on every keystroke.
Onboarding form state lives in Jotai atoms, grouped by step, with atomFamily used for per-field validation and a selectAtom derived atom feeding the progress indicator.
Switched from SWR to TanStack Query v5 because the app needed mutation lifecycle hooks and query invalidation graphs that SWR could not express declaratively.
Server state is managed by TanStack Query v5 with a global QueryClient configured for 30s stale time, exponential retry backoff, and an Axios wrapper that normalizes error shapes.
Moved the darkraise-ui package from React Router v6 to TanStack Router to get end-to-end typed routes and file-based route generation.
The UI uses TanStack Router with file-based route generation, each route exposing loader, search params schema, and error boundary colocated, and a root route owning the auth guard.
Dropped hash-based routing on the embedded analytics widget after customers complained deep links broke when pasted into Slack unfurls.
The embedded widget uses the History API with a configurable basename so host apps can mount it under /analytics while retaining shareable deep links with standard URLs.
Replaced MUI v5 with shadcn/ui after designers could not override the deeply nested Emotion styles without escape-hatch sx props everywhere.
The component system is a copy-in shadcn/ui library on top of Radix primitives, styled with Tailwind and CVA variants, published internally as @darkraise/ui with tree-shakable exports.
Chose Mantine v7 over Chakra v2 for the internal tools after needing polished data grid, date range picker, and rich text editor primitives out of the box.
Internal tools use Mantine v7 with the Mantine DataTable, Mantine Dates, and Tiptap integration, themed by a single createTheme call driven from a design-token JSON file.
Adopted Style Dictionary for design tokens after hex values drifted between Figma, iOS, and the web app and caused three brand-inconsistency bug reports in a month.
Design tokens are authored in a single tokens.json, transformed by Style Dictionary into CSS variables, Tailwind theme extensions, Swift enums, and Kotlin objects consumed across platforms.
Moved the marketing codebase from Sass modules to Tailwind v3 after dead-style audits showed 38% of shipped CSS was unused on mobile.
Styling uses Tailwind v3 with a design-token preset, tailwind-merge for class reconciliation, and PurgeCSS running against MDX and TSX sources for a final 18 KB CSS bundle.
Switched from styled-components to vanilla-extract because runtime CSS-in-JS added 40 ms to hydration on the checkout route.
Styles compile at build time via vanilla-extract with static theme contracts, generating atomic CSS through Sprinkles and ship zero runtime JS for styling in the checkout bundle.
Replaced Formik with react-hook-form in the signup funnel after re-render storms on large field arrays caused dropped keystrokes on low-end Chromebooks.
Signup forms use react-hook-form with uncontrolled inputs, Zod resolvers for validation, and a FormProvider at each step so field-array rows rerender in isolation.
Adopted Zod schemas shared across client and server after duplicate yup and Joi validators drifted and rejected valid submissions on the edge.
Form schemas are defined once in a shared @darkraise/schemas package using Zod, consumed by react-hook-form resolvers on the client and by Fastify route validation on the server.
Replaced localStorage JWT storage with httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies after a dependency with a postinstall script exfiltrated tokens in a preview build.
The SPA authenticates against a same-origin /auth proxy that sets httpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict session cookies, with CSRF tokens issued per form and verified by the API gateway.
Adopted Auth.js (NextAuth v5) over a hand-rolled OIDC client because refresh-token rotation and multi-provider linking kept regressing under test.
Authentication in the Next.js app is managed by Auth.js v5 with the Prisma adapter, Keycloak and GitHub providers, and middleware gating every /app route on a valid session cookie.
Switched the legacy webpack 5 pipeline to Rspack after production builds consistently exceeded the nine-minute CI budget on large branches.
The build pipeline runs Rspack 1.0 with the webpack-compatible config, SWC loaders, persistent filesystem cache on the CI runner, and a module-federation remote for the plugin surface.
Chose Rollup over Vite library mode for the published UI package because we needed multi-format output plus bundled .d.ts files with precise export maps.
The @darkraise/ui package is built by Rollup 4 emitting ESM and CJS bundles, dts-rollup-generated type bundles, and a package.json with fine-grained exports per component entry.
Replaced Jest with Vitest after ESM-only dependencies broke the transform pipeline and ts-jest startup took 11 seconds on a two-test file.
Unit tests run under Vitest 1.6 in happy-dom mode, parallelized with eight workers, sharing the Vite dev config so module resolution matches the production bundle exactly.
Migrated E2E tests from Cypress to Playwright after flake on cross-origin iframes and a missing multi-tab model made auth-flow tests unreliable.
E2E suites run in Playwright with three projects (chromium, firefox, webkit), sharded across four CI runners, using a storageState fixture to skip login for non-auth scenarios.
Adopted Chromatic for visual regression after three UI bugs shipped to production that a diff would have caught before review.
Storybook 8 stories are published to Chromatic on every PR, with baseline snapshots keyed on the main branch, TurboSnap enabled to skip unchanged components, and a required GitHub check.
Chose Playwright's toHaveScreenshot over a SaaS visual tool because we already ran Playwright in CI and did not want another vendor managing screenshot baselines.
Visual regression runs as a dedicated Playwright project with deterministic fonts, masked timestamps, and PNG baselines stored in Git LFS under tests/visual/__screenshots__.
Adopted axe-core in CI after a customer audit flagged 14 WCAG 2.2 AA violations that had slipped through manual review for a year.
Accessibility checks run as a Playwright project invoking axe-core on every key page, failing CI on serious or critical impact rules and producing a HTML report published as a job artifact.
Chose the Storybook addon-a11y to shift accessibility left after most issues originated at the component level rather than the page composition.
Every Storybook story runs the addon-a11y checks in the Storybook test-runner under axe, with a shared axe config that disables color-contrast on tokens-sourced swatches.
Switched from i18next to FormatJS after translators complained about missing ICU plural and select support on the billing invoices page.
Localization uses FormatJS with ICU MessageFormat strings, messages extracted to JSON by formatjs extract, and language bundles loaded on demand with dynamic import() per locale.
Moved locale resolution from the client to the edge after users hitting the German site briefly saw English content while the bundle loaded.
Locale is detected at a Cloudflare Worker by Accept-Language and a user cookie, injected into the HTML as a __LOCALE__ global, and consumed by React Intl providers during SSR hydration.
Adopted LaunchDarkly over env-variable gates after the pricing experiment needed percentage rollouts and per-account targeting within a single deploy.
The SPA bootstraps LaunchDarkly on mount with user identity keyed on account_id, streams flag updates via SSE, and wraps gated UI in a FeatureFlag component that short-circuits render.
Chose OpenFeature with flagd for internal tool flags because data residency rules blocked sending user identifiers to a SaaS flag provider.
Internal web apps evaluate flags through the OpenFeature React SDK against a flagd sidecar at localhost:8013, with rule definitions synced from a Git repository and reloaded on change.
Replaced Google Analytics 4 with self-hosted PostHog after EU privacy review required first-party telemetry and session replay without third-party cookies.
Client analytics call a self-hosted PostHog instance via a reverse-proxied /ingest path, with autocapture enabled, session replay sampled at 10%, and identify fired after login.
Adopted Segment with server-side destinations after ad blockers dropped about 22% of client-side events on the marketing funnel.
Events are sent client-side to a same-origin /collect edge endpoint that forwards to Segment server-side, which fans out to Mixpanel, Braze, and a BigQuery destination.
Adopted nested React Error Boundaries tied to Sentry after a single uncaught render error in the sidebar blanked the entire dashboard for five minutes.
The app wraps each top-level route and each async island in an ErrorBoundary that reports to Sentry with a scoped tag and renders a localized fallback UI with a retry button.
Enabled Sentry Session Replay on error-only sampling after support could not reproduce intermittent drag-and-drop bugs reported by enterprise users.
The SPA configures Sentry browser SDK with replaysSessionSampleRate=0 and replaysOnErrorSampleRate=1, masking all text inputs and blocking screenshots on the compliance-flagged routes.
Adopted React 19 streaming SSR with Suspense boundaries after the product page's server render blocked on a slow reviews call, delaying Time To First Byte by 900 ms.
Product pages stream through React 19 renderToPipeableStream with Suspense boundaries around reviews, recommendations, and inventory, each resolved independently from the backing service.
Chose route-level lazy() boundaries over component-level after bundle analysis showed admin-only views were loaded for every signed-in customer.
Every TanStack Router route component is imported via lazy() with a shared Suspense boundary showing a skeleton, and router-level preload runs on link hover for primary navigation.
Moved the dashboard from REST to GraphQL with a single endpoint because the widgets page made 14 sequential calls that could not be parallelized cleanly.
The dashboard queries a federated GraphQL gateway through urql with Graphcache, persisted operation IDs, and a single websocket subscription channel for live widget updates.
Chose tRPC over a hand-written REST client for the internal admin app because the teams own both ends of the wire in the same TypeScript monorepo.
The admin app calls a tRPC v11 router over HTTP batch links, types shared from the backend package, and uses superjson transformers so Date and Decimal values round-trip unchanged.
Adopted React Server Components in the Next.js app for the reporting surface after client-only data fetching left large hydration payloads on routes nobody interacted with.
Reporting pages render as Server Components that fetch from Postgres directly through a server-only data layer, with Client Components pushed to leaves like filters and chart legends.
Adopted Workbox-generated service workers after field technicians in low-connectivity warehouses lost form progress when the Wi-Fi dropped mid-shift.
The field-ops PWA uses a Workbox service worker with a StaleWhileRevalidate strategy for APIs, a CacheFirst strategy for shell assets, and a background sync queue for pending form POSTs.
Chose IndexedDB via Dexie over localStorage for the draft editor because quotas and write latency on localStorage broke autosave for documents over 1 MB.
Drafts are persisted to IndexedDB through Dexie 4 with a versioned schema, an autosave hook debounced at 400 ms, and a background reconciliation worker that diffs local drafts against the server.
Picked Nx for the frontend monorepo over Turborepo because the team needed generators, module-boundary lint rules, and a dependency graph visualizer on day one.
The frontend monorepo is organized with Nx 19, enforcing tag-based import boundaries between feature, ui, and data-access libs, with Nx Cloud remote cache shared across developers and CI.
Replaced a 240 KB icon font with tree-shakable SVG React components via SVGR after the font blocked First Contentful Paint on slow 3G.
Icons are authored as SVG files, compiled by SVGR into typed React components with aria-hidden defaults, and imported per-icon so only referenced glyphs land in the route bundle.
Chose visx over Recharts for the finance dashboard because dense time-series plots needed bespoke axes and Canvas fallback for 40k-point series.
Finance charts are composed from visx primitives on top of a shared scale provider, SVG for <5k points and a Canvas renderer above that threshold, with a d3-time axis shared between both paths.
Adopted Framer Motion over CSS keyframes for route transitions after designers needed shared-layout animations between the list and detail views.
Route transitions use Framer Motion's layout animations, with a LayoutGroup at the router outlet and AnimatePresence wrapping the route tree so exit animations run before unmount.
Replaced react-dnd with dnd-kit on the kanban board after keyboard-only users could not reorder cards and the HTML5 backend dropped on touch devices.
The kanban board uses dnd-kit with the sortable preset, keyboard and pointer sensors configured, a DragOverlay rendered outside the scrollable column, and accessible announcements on drop.
Switched from react-window to TanStack Virtual on the audit log page because variable row heights and a sticky group header caused visible jumps on scroll.
The audit log uses TanStack Virtual's useVirtualizer with dynamic row measurement, overscan of 8, and a sticky group header rendered outside the virtualized range to avoid measurement drift.
Turned on TypeScript strict mode across the SPA after three production incidents traced back to undefined prop access that PropTypes warnings did not catch in production builds.
The SPA compiles with tsconfig strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and verbatimModuleSyntax, with a project-references graph splitting app, ui, and data-access layers.
Switched from npm to pnpm for the frontend workspace after node_modules size on a fresh clone exceeded 2.1 GB and installs took over four minutes.
The workspace uses pnpm 9 with a content-addressable store, a locked packageManager field in root package.json, and a .npmrc enforcing public-hoist-pattern=[] to catch phantom deps.
Adopted ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint v8 after the legacy .eslintrc chain across packages drifted and produced inconsistent rules per workspace.
Linting runs from a single eslint.config.mjs at the monorepo root with scoped overrides per package, typescript-eslint v8 type-aware rules, and a Prettier disabled-rules block to avoid conflicts.
Switched the SFT pipeline from DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 to PyTorch FSDP after memory fragmentation killed the last two 70B runs past step 4000.
SFT jobs run on 8xH100 nodes with PyTorch FSDP full-shard strategy, bf16 mixed precision, gradient checkpointing on every other transformer block, and Weights & Biases for metric streaming.
Adopted 4-way tensor parallelism on top of data parallel after single-GPU activation memory for the 34B model spilled into host RAM and wrecked throughput.
The 34B pretraining topology uses TP=4 within each 8-GPU node and DP=16 across nodes, with NCCL over a 400 Gb/s InfiniBand fabric and activation recomputation in every MLP block.
Picked Lion over AdamW for the 7B continued-pretrain run after an ablation showed comparable loss at 40% less optimiser state memory.
Continued-pretraining uses the Lion optimiser at lr=3e-5 with beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99, weight_decay=0.1, and a distributed ShardedOptimizer wrapper checkpointed every 1000 steps.
Moved the pretraining corpus from Hugging Face streaming to WebDataset shards on S3 after DataLoader stalls throttled effective throughput below 45% MFU.
Pretraining data lives as 8 GB WebDataset tar shards on S3, prefetched by a torchdata DataPipe with 16 worker processes per node and a 2 GB on-disk local cache for hot shards.
Decided to retrain the SentencePiece tokenizer from scratch on the code-heavy mix after OOV rate on Rust and Solidity files exceeded 11% with the inherited Llama tokenizer.
The tokenizer is a 64k-vocabulary SentencePiece unigram model trained on 120 GB of deduplicated code and prose, with byte fallback enabled and NFC normalisation applied before encoding.
Locked the whole training stack to bf16 after fp16 runs on the reward model diverged twice at step 9000 with loss-scale underflow.
All forward, backward, and optimiser-update passes run in bf16 on H100 tensor cores, with master weights kept in bf16 and no GradScaler since dynamic loss scaling is disabled.
Adopted torch.distributed.checkpoint asynchronous saving after synchronous full-state checkpoints stalled the job for 90 seconds every 2000 steps.

Checkpoints are written every 2000 steps through torch.distributed.checkpoint in async mode to a dedicated S3 bucket with per-rank sharded tensors and a single metadata file resolved by the coordinator rank.
Standardised on EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness over an in-house eval script after two engineers reported different MMLU numbers on the same checkpoint.

Offline evals run lm-evaluation-harness v0.4 inside a pinned container on a dedicated 2xA100 box, scoring MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K, and TruthfulQA with a fixed seed and loglikelihood requests.
Picked Ray Tune with ASHA over a grid search after the twelve-point learning-rate sweep ate three weeks of GPU time for no meaningful gain.
Hyperparameter search runs Ray Tune 2.10 with the ASHA scheduler over 64 concurrent trials on a dedicated 4-node A100 cluster, reporting into a shared MLflow tracking server.
Migrated experiment tracking from local TensorBoard event files to Weights & Biases after cross-run comparisons across branches became impossible to share with reviewers.

Every training job streams metrics, system stats, and artefact manifests into Weights & Biases under the darkmem-llm project, with per-branch groups and per-run config hashes for deterministic replay.
Moved model artefacts from an NFS share to a content-addressed S3 layout after two engineers overwrote each other's checkpoints on the same path.
Final and intermediate checkpoints live under s3://darkmem-artefacts/ keyed by sha256 of the state_dict manifest, with a sqlite index mapping run_id, step, and git_sha to the corresponding S3 prefix.
Chose a Bradley-Terry pairwise reward model over a pointwise scalar regressor after inter-annotator agreement on absolute scores collapsed below 0.4 kappa.
The reward model is a 7B transformer with a scalar head trained on 180k Bradley-Terry preference pairs, using a margin-ranking loss with beta=0.1 and a 10% chosen/rejected swap regulariser.
Swapped the PPO rollout loop for DPO after PPO hyperparameter sensitivity caused three consecutive runs to collapse into repetition within 500 steps.
The alignment stage is a single-phase DPO run over 120k preference pairs with beta=0.1, reference model frozen in bf16, and a constant lr=5e-7 schedule over 3 epochs.
Adopted the TRL SFTTrainer over a hand-rolled Trainer subclass after the packing and response-only loss masking code kept drifting between the chat and code variants.
SFT runs on TRL 0.9 SFTTrainer with sequence packing enabled at 8192 tokens, DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM masking the prompt, and a Hugging Face Accelerate launcher for FSDP configuration.
Chose QLoRA with 4-bit NF4 quantisation for the instruction-tune experiments after full fine-tune on the 13B base blew the 80 GB VRAM budget per GPU.

Instruction tuning uses QLoRA with bitsandbytes NF4 quantisation, LoRA adapters of rank 64 and alpha 16 on all linear layers, paged AdamW 8-bit optimiser, and merged weights exported to safetensors at the end.
Set DPO beta to 0.05 for the safety-tuned variant after higher beta values made the model refuse benign prompts at a 9% false-positive rate on the internal eval set.

The safety DPO run trains the 7B SFT checkpoint for two epochs at beta=0.05 over 60k harmlessness-preference pairs, with ref_model shared across ranks and reported win-rate on a held-out 2k-prompt slice.
Adopted a fast slice-eval every 250 steps after full MMLU at checkpoint time meant regressions were only caught after an eight-hour run completed.

Training launches a sidecar eval worker that every 250 steps runs a 500-example slice covering MMLU-STEM, GSM8K-100, and an internal refusal probe, reporting deltas back into the W&B run as custom charts.
Enabled early stopping with patience 5 on eval perplexity after three long runs overfit past step 18k with no validation-loss improvement for 10k steps.
The SFT trainer uses a patience-5 early-stopping callback on held-out eval loss, checkpointing the best state and aborting the remainder of the schedule when patience is exhausted.
Raised gradient accumulation from 4 to 16 after reducing micro-batch size to fit the 70B model, targeting a constant global batch size of 1024 sequences.
The 70B SFT run uses a per-device micro batch of 1, gradient accumulation of 16, and 64-way data parallelism for a fixed global batch of 1024 sequences, with all-reduce fused into the backward pass.
Switched from linear decay to a cosine schedule with a 2% warmup after the earlier run's loss curve showed a sharp plateau at the 40% mark of training.
The learning-rate schedule is a single cosine decay from lr=2e-5 to 2e-6 over 30k steps with a 600-step linear warmup, implemented via transformers.get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup.
Added a MinHashLSH near-dedup pass over the raw web crawl after a memorisation probe showed 2.3% of training strings appeared verbatim in held-out eval prompts.
The pretraining data pipeline runs a Spark MinHashLSH job with 128 permutations and Jaccard threshold 0.8, emitting a deduplicated Parquet dataset keyed by document hash before tokenisation.
